transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me a little bit about what has been bothering you and what brings you in to see me today?

I'm just really distressed about how awful my face looks right now. I have these terrible acne scars and blemishes all over my skin, and it feels like it's all anyone sees when they look at me. I just can't bear looking like this anymore and really need some help.

Do you find yourself spending a significant amount of time each day performing repetitive behaviors like checking your skin in mirrors, picking at your face, or seeking constant reassurance about your appearance?

Yes, I do all of those things constantly. I compulsively check every single mirror I pass and find myself picking at my skin to try and 'fix' the flaws. I also keep asking my family for reassurance that I don't look horrible, but even when they tell me I look fine, it never actually makes me feel any better.

latest_inference.note: The patient's description of persistent distress regarding perceived skin flaws, combined with repetitive behaviors such as mirror checking, skin picking, and constant reassurance seeking—despite reassurances from others—is highly characteristic of Body Dysmorphic Disorder. Given the focus of the clinical presentation, Major Depressive Disorder is less likely to be the primary diagnosis, though it may be comorbid; however, the clinical picture is now sufficiently specific to narrow the primary diagnosis to Body Dysmorphic Disorder.
